newsitem.title: UK: Coconut oil closes sharply down on European market.
newsitem.headline: Coconut oil closes sharply down on European market.

text.p: Coconut oil prices were sharply lower at the close of business in Europe on Wednesday.
In trading largely by dealers, selling levels dropped by as much as $20 a tonne, but traders said the fall was not as dramatic as it looked.
"The market hasn't done a lot recently so in a way it has been catching up today," said one.
Palm oil prices closed lower following profit-taking in Kuala Lumpur during the European morning.
Traders said the market was looking over bought, but in the short term at least, the bull run was not over.

Traders believe India will only remain in the market until its own vegetable oil crops start to come in during November and China is unlikely to do any substantial buying of palm oil while the price remains high.
Soft oils had been supported by a firm Chicago market on Tuesday but towards the close sellers had started to back track as the U.S. market came in lower.
However, business remains slow with buyers not keen to take fresh positions as most refiners seem to be comfortable and happy to sit the weather market out for the time being.

At the close coconut oil was $10 to $20 down after Jul/Aug traded at $760, Aug/Sep $725, Sep/Oct $710, Oct/Nov $705 and Nov/Dec at $700 a tonne cif. Traders said all these prices has been paid a number of times.
In the remainder of the market no further business was reported.
Crude palm oil closed unchanged to $5 down while refined palm oil was $2.50 to $7.50 lower.
Soft oils closed with soy oil unchanged to 0.50 guilder down and rape oil mixed at two guilders up to 0.25 guilder lower.
